prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Charlotte. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Charlotte for a dental implant?
competitors_mentioned: South Charlotte Oral, Facial & Implant Surgery
Carolinas Center for Oral & Facial Surgery
answer_verbatim:
For a Charlotte implant, I’d start with **two surgical consultations** and make sure the office has a clear plan for the final crown/bridge—not just placement of the implant.

### Practices to call

| Practice | Why call them | Best fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Carolinas Center for Oral & Facial Surgery (CCOFS)** | Large Charlotte-area oral and maxillofacial surgery group that handles implant placement, extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts, and sedation. A strong first call if your case may involve an extraction, limited bone, or multiple implants. | Most routine-to-complex implant cases; patients who want an oral surgeon and sedation option. |
| **South Charlotte Oral, Facial & Implant Surgery** | Implant-focused oral-surgery practice in the south Charlotte area. Worth comparing with CCOFS for the surgeon’s treatment plan, grafting recommendation, timing, and total surgical cost. | South Charlotte/Ballantyne-area patients; single implants, extractions with immediate implant planning, and grafting cases. |
| **Metrolina Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery** | Another Charlotte-area OMS option for an independent surgical opinion. An oral surgeon is particularly useful when the tooth must be removed, you have infection, need a graft, or are considering full-arch treatment. | North/central Charlotte patients and anyone wanting a second surgical opinion. |
| **Atrium Health Carolinas Medical Center – Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery** | Consider this route if you have significant medical issues—such as complex heart/lung disease, anticoagulants, cancer treatment history, difficult anesthesia concerns, or a highly complicated reconstruction. Hospital-based care can be valuable in those situations. | Medically complex or reconstructive cases; may require referral and may not be the simplest route for a routine implant. |

### My practical recommendation

1. **Call CCOFS first** for a comprehensive implant-surgery consultation.  
2. **Call South Charlotte Oral, Facial & Implant Surgery or Metrolina OMS for a second opinion**, especially if you are told you need bone grafting, a sinus lift, multiple implants, or “same-day/All-on-X” treatment.  
3. Before surgery, choose the dentist or prosthodontist who will make the **final crown, bridge, or denture**. The long-term result depends heavily on that restorative plan.

For a straightforward single missing tooth, your regular dentist may coordinate the crown after an oral surgeon places the implant. For a front tooth, several missing teeth, a failed implant, bite problems, or full-mouth work, I would strongly consider having a **prosthodontist** involved before the implant is placed.

### What to ask when you call

Use these questions to quickly separate a thorough implant office from a sales-focused one:

- “Will the surgeon use a **3-D CBCT scan** to plan the implant?”
- “Who will design and place the final crown or bridge, and will that provider be involved **before surgery**?”
- “Do I need extraction, bone grafting, a membrane, or a sinus lift—and why?”
- “Can I receive a written estimate that separates the **scan, extraction, graft, implant, abutment, crown, temporary tooth, and sedation**?”
- “What implant system do you use, and will replacement components be readily available in the future?”
- “If I have a complication or implant failure, what follow-up care is included?”
- “Does the surgeon perform this type of case routinely?”
- “Can you submit estimates to my dental and medical insurance?”

### Important cost point

Dental insurance often covers part of an extraction, graft, or crown but may not cover the implant itself. Ask for the **complete start-to-finish price**. A quote that sounds inexpensive may exclude the crown, graft, temporary tooth, CT scan, or sedation.

I can’t verify current appointment availability, insurance participation, or each office’s current providers as of November 2026, so confirm those details directly. But for most Charlotte residents, **CCOFS plus one of South Charlotte Oral, Facial & Implant Surgery or Metrolina OMS** is a sensible first round of consultations.
